messages.content: Client finally answered for Denver. It is Greenwood Village, near the Denver Tech Center, Tuesday starts at 9, and Monday evening setup is optional now. Can you compare the flight and hotel combinations again and help me pick what to send for approval?

Yes. With the office in Greenwood Village/DTC and no required Monday setup, I would stop optimizing for the absolute cheapest arrival and focus on getting you rested and close to the client Tuesday morning. The main tradeoff is: pay a bit more for the Monday Delta nonstop plus the closer business hotel, or save on the one-stop flight and suite hotel but accept a late arrival and a longer Tuesday commute.
The address is just off Belleview and Quebec. No hotel block. They said there may be a team dinner but it is not confirmed.

For that address, the stronger approval package is: Monday ATL-DEN Delta nonstop, about 2:10 PM to 3:40 PM, then the closer DTC hotel. You would likely reach the hotel before 5:15, have time for dinner, and not need a car. The cheaper package is a one-stop itinerary landing close to 9:50 PM, then the suite-style hotel with breakfast included. It saves roughly $150 to $190 total, but pushes hotel arrival toward 11 and adds connection risk in winter.
The one-stop is tempting if finance looks closely. How bad is it operationally?

I would call it a false economy for this workshop. The one-stop has one connection, but the arrival time is the problem: by the time you deplane, get a rideshare, and reach DTC, you are eating dinner late or skipping it. If the connection slips, Tuesday morning gets uncomfortable. The nonstop gives you a normal evening and removes the transfer risk.
Okay. Walk me through the hotels again.

Closer hotel: Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center, strong guest rating around 4.2, on-site restaurant, good rideshare access, about 7 to 10 minutes from Belleview/Quebec in normal traffic. Breakfast is paid, not included. Suite option: Homewood Suites/Denver Tech Center area, rating around 4.4, included breakfast and more room, but more like 18 to 25 minutes to the client in morning traffic and less useful for a late Monday dinner. For a 9:00 client start, I would take the closer hotel and treat breakfast as a manageable expense.
Will the paid breakfast be an approval issue? They have been picky lately.

I would flag it plainly rather than hide it: breakfast is not included, but the property is selected for proximity to the client office and lower commute risk. If the policy reimburses meals by receipt or per diem, this is fine. If breakfast inclusion is mandatory, then the suite option is the fallback, but you would be buying that with time each morning.
What about a rental car? I have not decided.

I would skip the rental unless the team dinner becomes offsite or they ask you to move between locations. For this address, rideshare is simpler: no parking question, no winter driving, and clean receipts. The closer hotel also makes rideshare more defensible because you are not taking long trips back and forth each day.
For Thursday, I still have not seen a final debrief time. It sounds like it should end by lunch.

Then you have two reasonable return choices. The mid-afternoon nonstop DEN-ATL, around 2:40 PM, is efficient and gets you home around 7:30 PM, but it assumes you can leave DTC by about 11:45 or noon. The early evening nonstop, around 5:55 or 6:05 PM, gives much more cushion but gets you back to Atlanta close to 11 PM. I would send the mid-afternoon return for approval only with a note that it depends on the debrief ending by lunch.
I do not want it to look like I am leaving early if the room is still working.

That is the one real downside of the mid-afternoon option. If you want the least awkward plan, choose the evening nonstop now. If you want the cleanest travel day and the client confirms a noon wrap, choose mid-afternoon. Since they said lunch is likely but not final, I would ask for the mid-afternoon return with that caveat and be ready to switch if the agenda moves.
Let us send the cleaner package but include the caveat. I need a short approval blurb.

Recommended plan is ATL-DEN nonstop Monday afternoon on Delta, DTC-area hotel near the Greenwood Village client office, and DEN-ATL nonstop Thursday mid-afternoon pending the final debrief end time. This avoids a late Monday arrival and reduces Tuesday morning commute risk. Rental car is not included; rideshare should be sufficient unless the client confirms offsite travel.
Add the hotel and cheaper alternatives in one line.

Add this: Hotel recommendation is the Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center on a refundable rate; breakfast is not included, but the property has on-site dining and the shortest commute. Lower-cost alternatives either add a flight connection with a late arrival or include breakfast at a suite property farther from the client, increasing morning commute variability.
Good. Please queue that for approval and do not book until it clears.

Queued for approval, not booked: Monday afternoon Delta nonstop ATL-DEN, Thursday mid-afternoon nonstop DEN-ATL with the debrief caveat, Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center refundable rate, and rideshare instead of a rental car. I also noted that the hotel does not include breakfast and that the less expensive options add either a connection, a late arrival, or a longer morning commute. Once it clears, I will lock seats and recheck the Thursday timing.

messages.content: Manager approved the Monday Delta nonstop and the Hyatt DTC, with rideshare instead of a rental. Now the client moved the Thursday debrief later, probably ending around 1:30 or 2. Should I change the return before the fare moves?

Yes, I would change it. The 2:40 PM DEN-ATL nonstop only works if you can leave the client by about 11:45, and the updated debrief makes that unrealistic. The later Delta nonstop around 5:55 PM gives you time to finish, get out of DTC around 3:15, and still have a sane airport buffer. The one-stop returns I see do not save enough to justify adding a connection.
How much more is the later nonstop than the one already approved?

It is about $96 more than the approved mid-afternoon fare. The cheapest one-stop is only about $35 less than the later nonstop, but it adds a connection and gets you home at about the same or later. I would not choose that for such a small savings.
Any reason to hold the mid-afternoon one and hope they finish early?

Only if the client confirms a firm noon stop today. Otherwise the risk is either leaving the debrief early or missing the flight. The later nonstop is the cleaner work decision even though it means a late Atlanta arrival.
Switch it. Give me one sentence I can send my manager about the fare increase.

Switched the return to the later nonstop DEN-ATL, departing about 5:55 PM and arriving Atlanta around 10:45 PM; outbound and hotel stay unchanged. Manager note: The client moved the Thursday debrief to a 1:30-2:00 PM finish, so I changed to the later nonstop to avoid leaving the session early; the fare increase is about $96, and one-stop options do not provide meaningful savings.

messages.content: Can you give me the final Denver checklist before I leave? Include airport timing, rideshare, meals, receipts, and whether any better window seats opened.

Confirmed plan: Monday afternoon nonstop ATL-DEN, Thursday later nonstop DEN-ATL, Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center, rideshare only. Light snow is possible on arrival evening, so the main buffer is on the Denver side. I will keep this practical: ATL timing, DEN pickup, hotel/dinner, Tuesday morning, receipts, and seats.
Carry-on only from Decatur. What time should I leave?

For the Monday afternoon departure, leave Decatur around 11:15 AM if traffic is normal. That should put you at ATL about two hours before departure without a checked bag. If rain or a crash slows the connector, move that up by 20 to 30 minutes. Check in before you leave home and keep the boarding pass in the app.
What should I expect after landing at DEN?

Follow the rideshare signs in the terminal and confirm the pickup door in the app before heading outside. DEN to the Tech Center is usually 35 to 55 minutes; with light snow, budget closer to an hour. At the hotel, check in, ask for the folio email setup, and use the on-site restaurant for dinner if the roads are messy. There are also nearby casual options if conditions are fine.
And Tuesday morning before the 9 o'clock start?

Breakfast is not included, so plan either the hotel cafe/restaurant or a quick nearby coffee stop. Order rideshare around 8:05 AM for the 9:00 client start; that gives room for a short ride plus building check-in. Bring ID, confirm the client entrance, and save the rideshare receipt right away.
Seats and receipt handling?

Seats: outbound window 18A is selected, and the later return has window 20F selected; no better forward window has opened, but recheck when check-in opens in case an exit-row or closer-in window releases. Receipts: keep itemized rideshare receipts, hotel folio at checkout, and meal receipts for any reimbursable breakfast/dinner. Monday morning, do one last weather and flight-status check before leaving for ATL.
